checks: Interpolating a near-peak section to a point at each projection endpoint gives the two s-power lower envelopes. Their integrals add to L times that section's volume divided by s+1. Zero-length sides contribute zero. The cone from a full endpoint section to a point attains equality, since its section at height u is scaled by exactly 1−u/L.

Every closed cap has a compact convex trace. Its slice profile is upper semicontinuous by reverse Fatou and log-concave by Brunn–Minkowski and weighted AM–GM on positive sections. The zero and singleton profiles cause no exceptional loss. In the accepted scalar formula take sampling density 1/h and phase −t/h, which gives samples t+hj and error h times the cap-profile peak.

The cap-profile peak is at most W even for a vertical cap retaining an entire grid fiber. Applying the same bound to the whole source gives A_h≥(1−η)A and the stated normalized bound after subtracting ratios. A fixed positive discrepancy b implies η≥b/(b+2) or η≥1, hence L/h≤(s+1)(b+2)/b.

An affine block map sends the actual grid to aG+c, section volumes to |det T| times themselves, and both ordinary and covolume-weighted sampled masses to |a det T| times themselves. The ratios are invariant even if a<0.
Source f525b2b4bb53c54e §2 (3)–(5) and its block affine calculation match the frozen statement; the draft specializes to closed caps.

dependencies.hypotheses_mapping: Use the scalar estimate (4), which is explicitly stated for any compactly supported upper semicontinuous log-concave function. The through-cap slice profile has those properties without the parent theorem's diffuse-section hypotheses. Take sampling density 1/h and phase −t/h, then multiply the scalar error by h.

overlap.comparison: Scalar estimate (4) supplies absolute quadrature error for the section profiles. It does not give the sharp lower A/(LW) factor, the projection-length relative criterion, or the block affine normalization.

Gives a general box-and-cell absolute cap error. For r=1 it uses a common box bound; it does not supply the sharp one-coordinate peak-to-total comparison or the dimension-only projection-length criterion.

readability: The phase sign is clear after substituting (j−(−t/h))/(1/h)=hj+t. The compactness argument also handles a positive slice on an endpoint of a closed cap.

summary: The sharp peak-to-total comparison, uniform relative closed-cap error, and affine invariance follow with the stated constants for every allowed one-coordinate grid.
